algorithm: Diffusion Policy backbone (DDPM training / DDIM inference) conditioned on a compact 3D point-cloud feature (small MLP + max-pool encoder) instead of image features
hand: Shadow Hand (Adroit, Bi-DexHands, DexDeform, DexMV domains); Allegro Hand (DexArt, HORA domains; also real Roll-Up/Dumpling/Drill); parallel gripper (MetaWorld; real Pour)
arm: Franka Arm (real-robot Allegro and gripper rigs)
sim: MuJoCo (Adroit, MetaWorld), IsaacGym (Bi-DexHands, HORA), Sapien (DexArt, DexMV), PlasticineLab (DexDeform)
success_criterion: success rate; 3 seeds per experiment, 20 episodes evaluated every 200 training epochs, mean of the highest 5 success rates per seed, mean+std reported across 3 seeds (Sec. IV-A)
headline_metric: success rate, relative improvement over image-based Diffusion Policy
headline_value: 72-task sim average 74.4+/-29.9% vs 59.8+/-35.9% for image-based Diffusion Policy (24.2% relative improvement, Table I); real robot 85.0+/-11.2% vs 35.0+/-25.0% (Diffusion Policy) / 20.0+/-12.2% (Diffusion Policy Depth), 10 trials/task (Table VIII)
human_data: real robot: 40 human-teleoperated demos/task (Allegro via vision-based retargeting, gripper/Franka via keyboard); most simulated 'demonstrations' are RL-agent rollouts (VRL3 for Adroit, PPO elsewhere), not human data -- only DexDeform (human-teleoperated) and MetaWorld (scripted) differ
paper_code_mismatch: the paper's prose states the network predicts the noise added to the data, but the shipped default config trains with prediction_type: sample (predicting the denoised action a^0 directly), not epsilon; the paper only qualifies this later in the same section (Fig. 7 ablates both).
note_gaps: The DDPM reverse-process equation and part of the Implementation Details paragraph are flattened around a table/figure block; code/md is a signature-only API map with no compute_loss body, so the loss is confirmed from paper prose plus the shipped scheduler config only.
